Subsequently he went toward the desert. After walking three days, he saw three anchorites, each one with a cross shining brighter than the Sun in his hand. He was blessed by them and asked them to guide him as to what he should do to save himself. They guided him to a valley which had fruitful trees and a spring of fresh water. He dwelt there persevering in prayers, and fasting. He ate from the fruits of the trees in the valley.

The devil fought him fiercely but the Saint overcame him with prayers and signing himself with the sign of the cross. He added to his worship until he reached a good old age.

When the day of his departure from this world drew near, the three hermits came to him. After praying together, they blessed each other then they told him, "The Lord had sent us to you to write down your biography for the benefit of others." He told them all that had happened to him. After a short illness he departed in peace. They prayed over him and buried him.

The blessing of his prayers be with us all and glory be to our God for ever. Amen.
04-14.title: The Departure of Saint Christodoulos, the Anchorite

04-15.html:
This day of the year 38 of the martyrs (322 A.D.) marks the departure of St. Gregory, the Patriarch of the Armenians who was a martyr, without bloodshed.

This saint was born about the year 257 A.D. in the capital of the province of Ararat in Armenia. His father’s name was Anak (Anash) of royal descent and he was put to death, but Gregory and his brother survived. Their caregiver fled away with them to Caesarea, Cappadocia, where she raised them in a life of piety and holiness. Gregory was adorned with many Christian virtues and he excelled in Philosophy and various subjects. Then he served in the royal court of king Tiridates.

One day, the King ordered him to offer sacrifice to the idols, however St. Gregory informed him that he was Christian. The King became full of fury and ordered to torture the Saint, but the Lord saved and healed him. Finally the King ordered to throw him in a deep pit to die there from thirst and hunger.

Near the pit lived an old widow, who saw, in a vision, someone telling her to make bread regularly and cast it into this pit. She continued to do so for 15 years. Because of the length of time, no one in his congregation knew if he was alive or dead.

When king Tiridates killed Arbsima, the virgin, and all the virgins who were with her, he also ordered to cast their bodies away on the mountains. Later on he regretted what he had done for he wanted to marry St. Arbsima. Because of his great grief, some of his advisors suggested for him to go out for hunting to overcome his grief. While he was riding his horse, an evil spirit possessed him. He fell on the ground and started to bite his body. Great fear and crying was heard all over the royal palace.

The king's sister saw a vision on three consecutive nights. She saw the angel of the Lord telling her that unless she brought St. Gregory out of the pit, her brother would not be cured. The people were perplexed, since they believed that he was dead. They went to the pit and dropped a rope and called his name. When the saint moved the rope, they knew that he was still alive, and they pulled him out.

St. Gregory went to the king, prayed for him, and the Lord answered his prayer and healed the king. But he was not completely cured; a mark was left in his body to remind him of his painful past.

The Lord opened the eyes of the king and believed in the Lord Christ and was baptized along with all the people of his kingdom.

When the holiness of Gregory became well known, they asked the Archbishop of Cappadocia who ordained him a bishop for Armenia. He is considered to be the first to preach the Gospel in Armenia after the apostle St. Bartholomew.

He took interest in caring, teaching and exhorting the people for about thirty years with intense enthusiasm. He carried the torch of faith to many pagan nations nearby the Caspian Sea and went as far as the Caucasian mountains. The people of these nations believed at his hands. He taught, baptized them, and built churches for them. He ordained for them bishops and priests. He put down for them canons and the order of worship.

When he completed his good endeavor, he departed in peace.

The blessing of his prayers be with us all. Amen.
04-15.title: The Departure of St. Gregory, Patriarch of the Armenians

04-15.html:
On this day also, St. Lucas (Luke), the Stylite, departed. This saint was born in one of the Persian countries to Christian parents. They reared him up on the Christian morals. When he became a young man, he enlisted in the Roman army, was promoted up the ranks until he became a centurion.

Later on he longed for the solitary life and worship. He forsook the world, and became a monk in one of the monasteries in the East. When his virtues became known, they ordained him a priest for this monastery. He grew in the life of asceticism and perseverance in fasting and prayers. Then he dwelt on an elevated rock for three years.

One day he heard a voice calling him by his name commanding him to leave his place on that rock. He left at once and saw a cross of light guiding him until he came to a high mountain where he stayed for a period of time. Then he was also inspired by God to go to a village nearby Constantinople and dwelt on a rock in the form of a pillar for forty five years. He practiced a strenuous spiritual fight and God granted him the gift of prophesying and performing miracles. He healed all those who came to him. When he finished his holy endeavor departed in peace.

The blessing of his prayers be with us all. Amen.
04-15.title: The Departure of St. Lucas, the Stylite

04-15.html:
Today also marks the departure of the saint Anba Ezekiel. This saint was a native of the city of Armunt. He left his family and went up the Armunt mount where he met with some of the fathers the anchorites. They guided him to the life of seclusion and put on him the monastic Eskeem. This saint lived in the inner wilderness in austere asceticism and toiled in many spiritual works.

When he did not have a source of water nearby to drink from, he tried to dig a well. The angel of the Lord appeared to him saying; “The Lord had seen your many labors, henceforth the water will come out of the rock. He lived a good angelic life and when he finished his good endeavor departed in peace.

The blessing of his prayers be with us all and glory be to our God for ever. Amen.
04-15.title: The Departure of the saint Anba Ezekiel, a native of Armunt

04-16.html:
On this day, of the year 1349 B.C., the righteous Gideon, one of the Judges of Israel, departed. He was from the tribe of Manasseh and his father's name was "Joash". While Gideon threshed wheat in the winepress the angel of the Lord appeared to him and said, "The Lord is with you, you mighty man of valor." (Judges 6:12) Gideon said to him, "O my lord, if the Lord is with us, why then has all these hardships happened to us? And where are all His miracles which our fathers told us about saying, 'Did not the Lord bring us up from Egypt?' But now the Lord has forsaken us and delivered us into the hands of Midianites."(Judges 6:13-14)

Then the Lord turned to him and said, "Go in this might of yours and you shall save the Israelites from the hand of the Midianites. Have I not sent you?" So he said to Him, "O my Lord, how can I save Israel? Indeed my clan is the weakest in Manasseh and I am the least in my Father's house." The Lord said to him, "Surely I will be with you, and you shall defeat the Midianites as one man."

Then Gideon said to Him, "If now I have found favor in Your sight, then show me a sign that it is You Who talk to me. Do not depart from here, I pray, until I come to You and bring out my offering and set it before You."

When Gideon was assured of the truthfulness of his calling to fight the Midianites, he took with him too many men. The Lord told him decrease the number for the people who are with you are too many, lest Israel claim glory for itself saying my own hand has saved me. He kept decreasing the number until they counted only three hundred men. With this few number of men, Gideon overcame the Midianites. He captured much of the spoil, and became a judge for Israel for about forty years.

The Lord God was with Gideon in all that he did. He departed in peace and was buried in the tomb of his fathers.

The blessing of his prayers be with us all. Amen.
04-16.title: The Departure of the Righteous Gideon, One of the Judges of Israel

04-16.html:
On this day also is the commemoration of, St. Harouadj (Herwog), St. Ananias and St. Khouzi, who were from Akhmeem.

The blessing of their prayers be with us all. Amen.
04-16.title: The Martyrdom of Saints Harouadj, Ananias and Khouzi

04-16.html:
This day also of the year 20 of the martyrs (304) Sts. Eulogius and Arsenius, Patron saints of El-Hadid monastery in Akhmeem were martyred.

They were from Syria, came to Egypt and dwelt on the Akhmeem mount. When Arianus came to Akhmeem they confessed the Lord Christ before him. The governor ordered to hang them head down, then tied heavy stones to their legs and were thrown into the river. The Lord saved them from drowning and brought them safe to the shore.

Later on Arianus convened three court sessions to try to persuade them at times and threatened and promised them at other times to turn them away from their faith in the Lord Christ. Finally when he could not change their steadfastness in the faith, he ordered to behead them with the sword, so they received the crown of martyrdom.

The believers buried their bodies with great veneration and many miracles were manifested from them. El-Hadid monastery in Akhmeem was built for them.

The blessing of their prayers be with us all. Amen.
04-16.title: The Martyrdom of Sts. Eulogius and Arsenius, Patron Sts. of El-Hadid monastery in Akhmeem

04-16.html:
On this day also was the Martyrdom of St. Amsah of Qift (el-Qifty). When Arianus the governor of Ansena arrived to the coast of Qift, the pagan priests went out to meet him and boast before him saying; “There is no one in our city to mention the name of Christ” so he rewarded them with many gifts.

In the city there was a young Christian whose name was Amsah. He dwelt with his virgin sister, Theodora living and working in a small garden, donating what exceeded their needs. When Amsah heard what the pagan priests said, he rose and went to the city of Tkoou where he found the governor torturing the Christians. He cried out saying; “I am Christian.” The governor became angry and ordered to beat him with green Palm-leaf stalk. His blood flowed on the ground and he fainted so they cast him in prison. In the next morning they found him standing up praying.

The governor ordered to wrap him in a straw mat and cast him in the Nile River thus he delivered up his spirit and received the crown of martyrdom.

God prepared a crocodile and it grasped the mat and escorted it until it was cast ashore near the city of Qift. The angel of the Lord appeared to his sister during the night and told her about the honor that her brother had received and commanded her to go to the bank of the river to find a straw mat wherein the body of her brother was wrapped. She went and found as the angel told her. She recovered the body, shrouded and buried him with great honor.

The blessing of his prayer be with us all. Amen.
04-16.title: The Martyrdom of St. Amsah el-Quifty

04-16.html:
Also, on this day is the commemoration of the consecration of the church of St. James the Persian, known as the Sawn-Asunder.

This church is located beside the church of the martyr St. Mercurius Abu-Saifain in Old Cairo. The account of his martyrdom is under the 27th day of Hathor.

The blessing of his prayers be with us all and glory be to our God for ever. Amen.
04-16.title: The Consecration of the Church of St. James, the Persian

04-17.html:
On this day the church celebrates the commemoration of the relocation of the body of the great ascetic St. Lukas the Stylite.

When he departed on top of the pillar that he dwelt on nearby Constantinople, his disciples went and told the Patriarch about his departure. He took with him the priests, crosses and censers and went to where the body of the saint was. They carried him to Constantinople with hymns, praises and prayers. After they prayed over him, the believers received the blessing from his pure body. They placed him in a marble sarcophagus next to the bodies of the saints. God manifested many signs and miracles from his body.

The blessing of his prayers be with us all. Amen.
04-17.title: The Commemoration of the Relocation of the Body of St. Luke the Stylite

04-17.html:
On this day also was the departure of St. Elias, in Mount Bishouaou (Bash-waw). His father was a farmer. When Elias grew he became a monk in Shamah mount. He persevered in asceticism and reading the Holy Scriptures. He learned many scriptures by heart. He did many prostrations and he completed his spiritual strife in mount Bash-waw.

God manifested many healing signs by his hands. When he was sixty six years old, he departed in peace.

The blessing of his prayers be with us all and glory be to our God for ever. Amen.
04-17.title: The Departure of St. Elias, in Mount Bash-waw

04-18.html:
On this day, the relics of St. Titus, the disciple of St. Paul, were relocated from Crete to Constantinople at the order of Emperor Constantine the great.

The Emperor directed his attention to the churches in all parts of his empire, decorating them with icons and the precious relics of the saints, especially those churches in Constantinople.

He collected the relics of the holy apostles and whatever he found from the relics of the honored martyrs.

When he heard that the relics of St. Titus were on the island of Crete, he sent some priests there, who carried the relics with great honors befitting him and brought them to Constantinople.

The Emperor built a beautiful church for him where he placed his pure body therein. God honored this saint by manifesting many miracles and signs from his holy relics. The account of his departure is mentioned under the 2nd day of the Little Month.

The blessing of his prayers be with us all. Amen.
04-18.title: The Commemoration of the Relocation of the Relics of St. Titus to Constantinople

04-18.html:
On this day also, was the martyrdom of St. Heracleas and St. Philemon the priest.

The blessing of their prayers be with us all and glory be to our God forever. Amen.
04-18.title: The Martyrdom of St. Heracleas and St. Philemon the Priest

04-19.html:
on this day of the year 1191 of the martyrs (1474 A.D.) Pope Gabriel VI, the 91st Patriarch of Alexandria departed. He was born in a village called El-Ara-aba el-Madfounah, district of al-Baliyana. He became a monk in the monastery of St. Antony (Antonius) and was promoted in the monastery until he became its abbot.

After the departure of Pope Mettaos II, the bishops and the lay leaders (Archons) convened to choose the new pope. They selected this father for his many virtues. They consecrated him patriarch by the name Pope Gabriel VI.

He resided in the patriarchal residence (cell) in the antiquated church of the Virgin Mary in Haret Zuweila. The duration of his papacy was eight years and six months. It was dominated by peace and tranquility and the church was not disturbed by any difficulties. He went on rebuilding and restoring the churches and teaching his flock.

When he completed his good endeavor, he departed in peace. His funeral was celebrated in a solemn public procession from Haret Zuweila to el-Khandaq monastery of St. Roweis. He was entombed in the tomb of the patriarchs under the church of Anba Roweis.

The blessing of his prayers be with us all. Amen.
04-19.title: The Departure of Pope Gabriel VI, the 91st Pope of Alexandria

04-19.html:
On this day also the Holy Father Anba John, bishop of El-Berollos, departed. He was the one to gather the biographies of the Saints - The Synaxarium.

He was born to a goodly priest and a pious mother. They raised and reared him with the Christian demeanor. When his parents departed, St. John took the money they left and built a hostel for the sojourners and the sick. He personally served them.

Once, a monk visited him in that place and saw his good deeds and he praised him. He also talked to him about monasticism, its honor, and greatness. The saint’s heart became attracted to the monastic life. He sold all what he owned and distributed his wealth among the poor and the needy. He went to the wilderness of "Shiheet" (Scetis) where Anba Daniel the hegumen put on him the monastic Eskeem. He lived a righteous life and became known for his austere asceticism and ardent worship. The devils became envious of this so they painfully beat him. He was sick and bedridden for a period of time after which the Lord Christ healed him and made him victorious against their warfare.

Because of his many virtues, knowledge, and godliness they consecrated him a bishop of el-Berollos. He resisted the heretics and brought back many of them to the Orthodox faith.

Every time this saint went up to the sanctuary (Hekal) to celebrate the Divine Liturgy, his face would shine and his tears poured for he was beholding the heavenly hosts around the altar. Three times when he placed his finger in the chalice for signing he found it as hot as fire.

During his life this Holy Father started writing the Synaxarium. Anba Peter (Botros) el-Gamil bishop of Melig and Anba Mikhail bishop of Atreeb completed the work after him.

When the Lord wanted to relieve him from the labors of this world, He sent to him St. Antony and St. Macarius to tell him of the day of his departure. He called his people and commanded them with many useful advices, then departed in peace.

The blessing of his prayers be with us all and glory be to our God for ever. Amen.
04-19.title: The Departure of Anba John, Bishop of El-Berollos, Who Gathered the Biographies of the Saints (The Synaxarium)

04-20.html:
On this day of the year 520 B.C. the upright prophet Haggai, departed. This righteous man was a descendant of Aaron, the priest, and from the tribe of Levi. He was one of the twelve Minor Prophets. He was born in Babylon in exile. He returned to the land of Judah along with Zerubbabel in the first return from exile in the year 536 B.C.

This prophet directed his prophecies by the command of God to Zerubbabel, then to Joshua the son of Jehozadak, the high priest. He incited the Jews to complete the rebuilding of the temple. They had started rebuilding the temple after they returned from captivity, then they abandoned it to build their own homes. The prophet rebuked them saying, "Is it time for you yourselves to dwell in your paneled houses and this temple to be in ruins?” Those who were upright amongst the people of Israel feared the threats of the Lord and built the house of the Lord as they were supposed to. Haggai the prophet had announced to the people after they finished building it, that the Lord was pleased by that.

He prophesied also about the church of the New Testament which will be built on the foundation of the Desire of All Nations, the Lord Jesus Christ, and its spiritual glory will be splendid.

This prophet lived more than seventy years then departed in peace. He was buried in the tomb of the priests in Jerusalem.

The blessing of his prayers be with us all. Amen.
04-20.title: The Departure of Haggai the Prophet

04-20.html:
On this day also of the year 20 of the martyrs (304 A.D.) was the martyrdom of Abba Elias, bishop of El-Kosiah.

This Holy Father strove much in prayers and lived a godly life. One day a poor man came to him crying because he suffered injustice from the clerk of El-Kosiah. The saint went and admonished the clerk saying; “God speedily avenges for the poor, for He is the Father of the orphans and the Advocate of the widows. O my son pay attention to the salvation of your soul.” The clerk wept, regretted and knelt before the saint. He returned all what he took from this poor man and he became meek, merciful and loving to the poor and the needy.

When Arianus the governor heard of St. Elias and what he performed from miracles and signs he summoned him. He promised him with many honors if he raised incense to the idols. The saint replied saying;”I do not worship devils and you Arianus will be martyred in the name of Christ.” The governor became angry and tortured him with many tortures then ordered to behead him so he received the crown of martyrdom.

The blessing of his prayers be with us all and glory be to our God for ever. Amen.
04-20.title: The Martyrdom of Abba Elias, Bishop of El-Kosiah

04-21.html:
On this day the church celebrates the monthly commemoration of the pure Virgin St. Mary, the Mother of God.

Her intercession be with us all. Amen.
04-21.title: The Commemoration of the Pure Virgin St. Mary, the Theotokos

04-21.html:
On this day also of the year 61 A.D. St. Barnabas, one of the Seventy Apostles, was martyred. He was from the tribe of Levi and his name was Joses (Joseph). His family resided on the Island of Cyprus where he was born. When he became a young man his parents sent him to Jerusalem to learn the Jewish subjects. There he became a disciple along with Saul of Tarsus to Gamaliel, a teacher of the law, who was one of the great leaders of the Jewish thinkers.

After Barnabas finished his studies, he followed the Lord Who appointed him to be one of the Seventy Apostles. He received the gift of the Holy Spirit in the upper room with the disciples on the day of Pentecost. He was called Barnabas, which is translated “son of encouragement”, by the apostles. Having land, sold it, and brought the money and laid it at the apostles’ feet.

St. Barnabas was the one to introduce Saul of Tarsus to the Disciples and the church of Jerusalem. He assured, comforted and told them how Saul had seen the Lord on the road to Damascus, and that He had spoken to him.

The church in Jerusalem sent out the apostle Barnabas to Antioch when it learned that the Gentiles there had accepted the word of God. When Barnabas came and had seen the grace of God, he was glad, and encouraged them all that with purpose of heart they should continue with the Lord. For Barnabas was a good man, full of the Holy Spirit and of faith, and a great many people were added to the Lord.

When the field of ministry expanded, Barnabas went to Tarsus and brought his fellow student Saul to Antioch. So it was that for a whole year they assembled with the church and taught a great many people.

Then they went up to Jerusalem and had the offerings and donations of the believers of Antioch to the poor brethren dwelling in Judea because of the famine that took place during the days of Claudius Caesar.

On their return to Antioch they took with them Mark, Barnabas’ nephew. In Antioch, the Holy Spirit said to the Church: "Now separate to Me Barnabas and Saul for the work to which I have called them. Then, having fasted and prayed and laid hands on them, they sent them away." (Acts 13:1-3)

They went to Seleucia, and from there they sailed to Cyprus where they preached the word of God. They also had Mark as their assistant. They returned to Antioch after they had completed their first missionary journey.

From Antioch they went up to attend the council of Jerusalem because of the dispute regarding the circumcision. Then Barnabas and Paul returned to Antioch carrying the decree of the council.

At the beginning of the second missionary journey the apostle St. Paul chose to take Silas however St. Barnabas took with him St. Mark and sailed to Cyprus. They preached there and converted many of its people to the faith of the Lord Christ. The Jews resented St. Barnabas, and seized him. They brutally beat him, and then stoned him. Finally they burnt his body in the fire so he delivered up his pure soul and received the crown of martyrdom. His body remained whole and the fire did not scorch it. The apostle St. Mark came and carried the body, wrapped it, and buried it in a cave. His tomb is still located in the city of Salamis in Cyprus.

The blessing of his prayers be with us all and glory be to our God for ever. Amen.
04-21.title: The Martyrdom of St. Barnabas, One of the Seventy Apostles

04-22.html:
This day marks the commemoration of the honorable archangel Gabriel, the announcer, the consecration of his church in the city of Caesarea, Palestine, and the appearance of many miracles therein.

He was the angel who God sent to announce to Zacharias the priest the birth of St. John the Baptist. (Luke 1:8-22) The Lord also sent him to announce to the Virgin St. Mary with the dwelling of the Word of God in her for the salvation of the world. (Luke 1:26-38) Therefore, the church gave him the title; the angel of Annunciation (the Herald of Glad Tidings).

He is one of the seven Archangels standing before God interceding at all times for the human race. So let us celebrate a spiritual feast for him entreating the archangel Gabriel to intercede for us before God to grant us the forgiveness of our sins.

The blessing of his holy intercession be with us all. Amen.
04-22.title: The Commemoration of the Honorable Archangel Gabriel, the Announcer

04-22.html:
On this day also of the year 20 of the martyrs (304 A.D.) St. Pachom and Dalusham his sister were martyred. They were born to poor Christian parents. They worked in farming a land in the village of Soflaq, north of Akhmeem.

When Pachom was eighteen years old his father passed away and his mother was seven months pregnant with his sister. He worked for a rich man called Simon in his orchard in the village of Soflaq.

When Arianus the governor of Ansena arrived to Akhmeem to persecute the Christians, he sent his soldiers to a village called Shansheef to bring its Christians. On their way, at Soflaq, they found St. Pachom. They seized him and asked about his name. He replied saying; “I am Christian” and confessed the Lord Christ as Lord and Savior. The captain became angry and ordered his men to tie a heavy stone to his neck. Pachom asked for the help of God and stood up while the stone was hanging from his neck, and everyone was amazed. They took him to the governor after they had tied his legs to a calf which dragged him behind while they were severely beating him. His mother and sister were following him crying.

When they arrived before the governor, he tried to turn him away from his faith. When he failed, he ordered to beat him with whips made of cow’s hide until he fell on the ground as a dead man. Shortly after he stood and signed himself with the sign of the cross. He praised God that made him worthy to suffer for His name’s sake.

His sister Dalusham came forward and confessed her faith in the Lord Christ and she was only eight years old. The governor was amazed from her strong faith and great love for the Lord Christ. They beat her severely until she fell down on her face and her brother Pachom was praying for her. The governor ordered to place hot fiery coal on her chest and sides. Then they chained her neck with heavy iron fetters and cast her in a cauldron filled with boiling water. The angel of the Lord came down and opened the boiler and brought her out unharmed.

As for St. Pachom they pulled out the nails of his hands and feet and tormented him with different kinds of tortures. Many of the people present believed because of their endurance. Finally the governor ordered to behead them thus they received the crown of martyrdom.

The people of Soflaq came, took the two bodies, shrouded them and buried them with great veneration. A church was built after their names in the village of el-Sawamaa Sharq (east) about ten kilometers north east of Akhmeem. Their bodies are located beside the body of their uncle Anba Psote (Bisada) the martyred bishop of Psoi (Absai) in his monastery located twenty-five kilometers south of Akhmeem.

The blessing of their prayers be with us all. Amen.
04-22.title: The Martyrdom of St. Pachom and Dalusham his Sister

04-22.html:
On this day also of the year 332 of the martyrs (616 A.D.) the Holy Father Pope Anastasius, the 36th Pope of Alexandria, departed. He was educated in the School of Alexandria and worked as a judge in the royal court. Then he left his position and was ordained a priest for the church of Alexandria.

The believers increased their appreciation for him, honored, and truly loved him for what they saw of sincerity, wisdom and uprightness in him. All these characteristics were the best recommendation for him to be chosen patriarch after the departure of Pope Demianos.

After his consecration, he devoted a great attention for the church. He ordained many bishops and priests to fill the vacant posts. He built several new churches and regained the churches that were being taken over by the Chalcedonians. The Chalcedonian Patriarch was annoyed so he falsely accused him to the Emperor. The Emperor sent his orders to the Governor of Alexandria to seize some of the churches that under the auspices of the Patriarch Anastasius and to hand them over to the alien patriarch.

Pope Anastasius was saddened and went to the wilderness of Shiheet where he stayed for many days in fasting and prayers asking for divine intervention. Subsequently the emperor’s brother killed him and took over the throne. Pope Anastasius returned to Alexandria and persisted in teaching and exhorting the flock in person and through his books.

Because of his great knowledge and eloquence, he wrote a book every year. He remained on the patriarchal throne for twelve years during which he wrote twelve books and arranged them according to the Coptic alphabets as their titles. When he completed his good endeavor he departed in peace.

The blessing of his prayers be with us all and glory be to our God for ever. Amen.
04-22.title: The Departure of Pope Anastasius, the 36th Patriarch of Alexandria

04-23.html:
On this day, of the year 1040 B.C. the King and the great prophet David, the son of Jesse, departed.

He was the second king of Israel. He was from the tribe of Judah from the village of Bethlehem. God chose him a king over the children of Israel, a successor to Saul, the son of Kish, who deviated from the straight path. God commanded the Prophet Samuel to go to Bethlehem to anoint David a king of Israel.

God was with him in all his ways, for his purity of heart and his meekness. He saved him from the hands of Saul who wanted to kill him on several occasions.

King David was adorned with many other virtues as humility and perpetual prayers. God praised him by saying, "I have found David, the son of Jesse, a man after My Own heart, who will do all My will." (Acts 13:22) He is the author of the book of the Psalms which is full of useful and deeply spiritual teachings and many prophecies about the Lord Christ.

David's might and power were supported by the God of heaven. When he was young and while tending to his father's sheep, a bear and a lion attacked his sheep and David killed both the bear and the lion.

When the army of Israel faced the army of the Philistines, Goliath, the champion of the Philistines, whose height was six cubits and a span, and was armed by many arms defied the army of Israel for forty days. No one dared to go down to fight him.

When David came one day to visit and see his brothers fare he saw and heard Goliath defying the people of Israel. David became zealous with a divine jealousy and took permission from King Saul. He came forward to face Goliath and he chose for himself five smooth stones from the brook and his sling was in his hand. David said to Goliath, "You come to me with a sword, with a spear, and with a javelin. But I come to you in the Name of the Lord of hosts, the God of the armies of Israel, whom you have defied. This day the Lord will deliver you into my hand." David took out a stone and he slung it and he struck the Philistine in his forehead, so that the stone sank in his forehead and he fell on his face to the ground. David ran and stood over the Philistine, took his sword and cut off his head and removed the reproach of Israel. (I Samuel 17:45-54)

After the death of Saul David took over the affairs of the kingdom and he reigned over Israel for forty years. He relocated the ark of God from Shiloh to the City of David, Jerusalem. David lived for seventy years and when he finished his good endeavor departed in peace.

The blessing of his prayers be with us all. Amen.
04-23.title: The Departure of David, the Prophet and King

04-23.html:
On this day also, the struggling saint Timothy the anchorite, departed. He was born to Christian parents, who educated and raised him according to the church disciplines. When he became a young man he desired the monastic life. He became a monk in one of the monasteries. He loved the solitary life so he lived in a cell alone near the monastery. He lived there for some time, making a living from the work of his hands.

The devil tried to deceive St. Timothy by sending him a woman to buy his handiwork. Because of her frequent visits, a special relationship developed between them. They sat to eat together at one table. After a short time, the saint realized the trick of the devil to make him fall into sin. He remembered the hour of death and the dreadful judgment. Immediately, he arose and fled away from that place.

God guided him to another place with a spring of water and beside it a palm tree. He dwelt there persevering in his worship and asceticism. He reached a high level of spirituality. The wild beasts came to him and became his friends. This continued on for thirty years and when he finished his good strife departed in peace.

The blessing of his prayers be with us all and glory be to our God for ever. Amen.
04-23.title: The Departure of St. Timothy, the Anchorite

04-24.html:
On this day of the year 107 A.D. St. Ignatius, Theophorus, Bishop of Antioch, was martyred. The ecclesiastical Tradition tells us that he was the child that Jesus called, took in His arms, and then set him in the midst of the disciples and said, “Assuredly, I say to you, unless you are converted and become as little children, you will by no means enter the kingdom of heaven. Therefore whoever humbles himself as this little child is the greatest in the kingdom of heaven.”

When he grew, he became a disciple of St. John the Evangelist. When St. John was preaching in Asia Minor he travelled with him to many cities. The holy apostles consecrated him a bishop for Antioch. He had a prominent personality, and he was an apostolic man, of great authority, and was respected in the universal church after the apostles.

St. Ignatius had a long fruitful ministry in Antioch. He converted many to the knowledge of God, baptized them, and illumined them with the church subjects. He wrote seven letters full of profound spiritual teachings to: the Ephesians, the Magnesians, the Trallians, the Romans, the Philadelphians, and the Smyrnaeans and to St. Polycarp, Bishop of Smyrna.

When Emperor Trajan visited Antioch, the fame of Ignatius and his zeal to spread the Christian spirit among his people reached him. The emperor summoned Ignatius and asked him, “Are you the one they call Theophorus, who disobeys my commands and does not confess my gods?” The saint replied with courage and calmness, “Yes, I am he who has Jesus Christ within him, for He is the true God, and your gods are nothing but useless, solid, inanimate statues.” The Emperor invited him to offer a sacrifice for the gods; however, the Saint replied, saying, “I am a priest for Jesus Christ, to whom I offer the sacrifice every day, and I desire to offer Him my life as a sacrifice.”

Then the Emperor issued his sentence that Ignatius would be led to Rome to be thrown to the beasts before the Roman people during their festive celebrations, entertaining them by watching one of the great men of Christianity being devoured by ferocious beasts. The saint thanked God for the grace of martyrdom, and everyone bid him farewell with tears.

They embarked with him on a ship that sailed to Smyrna. There, his friend, the bishop of Smyrna, St. Polycarp, came in haste to embrace him with tears. The churches in Asia, along with its bishops and people, also came in haste to bid him farewell, which comforted him. Upon his departure from Smyrna, he sent them his pastoral epistles that were previously mentioned, thanking them for their care. He urged them to stay away from heterodox teachings, to remain united among themselves, and to obey those in authority in the church (the bishop). Ignatius encouraged them to be patient and steadfast in the faith. These epistles were abundantly rich with love for the Lord Christ, deep humility, and fatherly compassion. From Smyrna, he wrote his famous letter to the Romans, saying, “I am writing to all the churches, and I enjoin all that I am dying willingly for God’s sake, if only you do not prevent it. I beg you not to do me an untimely kindness. Allow me to be eaten by the beasts, which are my way of reaching God. I am God’s wheat, and I am to be ground by the teeth of wild beasts so that I may become the pure bread of Christ.”

When they arrived to Rome, he was led to the amphitheatre where the multitudes were assembled. He knelt down, offered himself a sacrifice to God, and supplicated the Lord to preserve His church. The wild beasts devoured him and rendered him into pieces. He called upon the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, delivered up his pure spirit and received the crown of martyrdom.

His two deacons Philemon and Aghathon gathered his remains and bones, wrapped them in linen and brought them to Antioch where it was entombed and many signs and miracles were manifested.

The blessing of his prayers be with us all and glory be to our God for ever. Amen.
04-24.title: The Martyrdom of St. Ignatius, Theophorus, Patriarch of Antioch

04-25.html:
On this day of the year 575 of the martyrs (859 A.D.), the blessed Saint Anba Yehness (John) Kama the priest, departed. This saint was a native of "Shubra-Manthou" of the region of "Sa-el-Hagar". His parents were pious Christians and he was their only child. They raised him on the Christian manners and taught him the church subjects.

They forced him to marry against his will. When he was alone with his wife, they prayed for a length of time then he said to her, "My sister, you know that the world and all its lusts will go away. Do you agree with me on keeping our virginity?" She replied saying, "This also is my wish and now the Lord has granted me what my heart desired."

They mutually agreed to live a life of celibacy. When they lay down on their bed, the angel of the Lord came and covered them with his wings. Because of their holiness, God planted a vine to cover their place of sleep as a sign of their purity. For what they did was above human nature and God's divine power and care kept and guarded them.

One day St. John said to his wife, "My sister, I desire to go into the wilderness to become a monk and I cannot do that without your permission." She gave him her permission and he placed her in one of the virgins' convents. There she became a virtuous nun and later on she became the abbess of the convent.

However, St. John, the angel of the Lord guided him to the wilderness of Scetis "Shiheet." There, he became a monk under the guidance of a holy elder called "Darudi" (Teroti) in the monastery of St. Macarius. He stayed with this saint learning from him moral excellence and various virtues until he received his last blessing. Then the angel of the Lord commanded him to go a little west of the monastery of St. John the Short and to build for himself a monastery there. He went and did as the angel commanded him. Three hundred monks gathered around him and he taught them the prayers, the praises and the monastic virtues.

One night, St. Athanasius the Apostolic appeared to St. John to encourage him. Another time, the pure virgin St. Mary appeared to him and told him, "This is my dwelling forever, and I shall be with your children as I have been with you and this monastery will be named after me." Then she gave him three golden dinars and told him, “Take these and keep them and the blessing of my Son Jesus Christ will be with you all forever.”

When St. John Kama completed his good demeanor, he departed in peace. His children the monks buried his pure body in his monastery with great veneration. Then his body was relocated to the monastery of St. Mary known as the Syrian monastery where his body is still present, a blessing for the monks and the visitors

The blessing of his prayers be with us all. Amen.
04-25.title: The Departure of St. John Kama (Khame), the Priest

04-25.html:
On this day also the Holy Father Anba Abshai (Bishay) of mount Toud, departed. He was an ascetic worshipper since his young age. He read often in the prophecy of Jeremiah the prophet to the point that he saw him in person often. He did not give his body any rest for his many vigils, prayers, and prostrations. When he finished his good endeavor departed in peace.

They placed his body in the church which had a well of water. The Lord manifested many signs and healings for all who used this water. His monastery still exists located in the region of Toud east of Armunt and is called the monastery of the Saints. Wherein also is the body of the Holy Father St. Pisentius.

The blessing of his prayers be with us all and glory be to our God for ever. Amen.
04-25.title: The Departure of St. Abshai of Mount Toud

04-26.html:
On this day, of the year 20 of the martyrs (304 A.D.), St. Anastasia, was martyred.

This saint was born in the city of Rome in the year 275 A.D., to a pagan father, who was from the noble men of the city, and a Christian mother. Her mother baptized her secretly without her father's knowledge and she raised her well. She nourished her daily with the Christian teachings until she was firm in her faith that became difficult to take it away from her. She had a priest as a guide to care for her spirituality without her father’s knowledge.

When she was of marrying age, her father wedded her to a pagan youth, against her wishes. St. Anastasia prayed fervently to the Lord Christ to separate her from this pagan youth who was away from the faith. During his absence, she went to visit those imprisoned for the sake of the faith. She ministered to them, comforted, and offered them whatever they needed. When her husband learned about this, he shut her in the house and placed guards around it. She continued to pray entreating God to save her from his hands. God answered her prayer and speeded up his death. She distributed her wealth among the poor, those imprisoned, and the fighters for the sake of their faith.

When her account reached "Florus", the Governor, he brought her and inquired about her religion. She confessed the Lord Christ and did not deny. He tried to entice her to forsake her faith by promising her many precious gifts. When she refused he punished her with various tortures. Then he ordered to drown her in the sea. However with the grace of God she came out of the sea unharmed. Later on the governor ordered that she be hung on a cross and to light a fire under her. They did as ordered until she delivered up her pure spirit and received the crown of martyrdom.

The blessing of her prayers be with us all. Amen.
04-26.title: The Martyrdom of St. Anastasia

04-26.html:
On this day also the church celebrates the commemoration of the consecration of the church of the two martyrs Anba Bishay and his friend Anba Peter. They were martyred on the fifth day of the month of Paone.

After the end of the era of persecution and the reign of the righteous Emperor Constantine, the faithful built a church in the city of Boha the birth place of Anba Bishay where his house was located. They decorated it nicely and with all splendors.

The church was consecrated on this day. A church after their names presently located in the city of Sadfa, the diocese of Abu Tig where their bodies are located. Another church after their names is located in the city of Zagazig.

The blessing of their prayers be with us all and glory be to our God forever. Amen.
04-26.title: The Consecration of the Church of the Two Martyrs Anba Bishay and Anba Peter

04-27.html:
On this day of the year 20 of the martyrs (304 A.D.), the Holy Father Anba Bisadi (Psote), the bishop of "Ebsay" (Psoi), was martyred. This saint was born in the city of Ebsay in Upper Egypt to Christian parents. They worked in farming and tending the sheep. They raised him in the fear of God and taught him the holy books. When Bisada grew he worked with his father in taking care of the sheep. During his work he recited the Psalms. He diligently read the holy bible, fasted and practiced ascetic works.

As a young man God revealed to him in a vision what would befall the church at the hands of Diocletian when he becomes an emperor.

The bishop ordained him a deacon. When he saw in him the faithful heart in his love for God Who is eager for the salvation of every soul, he commended to ordain him a bishop to succeed him. After the departure of the bishop, the people unanimously agreed on his ordination. The Patriarch agreed to fulfill their wish and he consecrated him a bishop. He increased in asceticism, worship and humility. God granted him the gift of performing miracles and other gifts. He used these gifts in shepherding the faithful and guiding them in the way of holiness, repentance, and enduring trials.

After Diocletian had denied the faith, he sent to Arianus, the governor of Ansena, a message asking him to offer to Anba Bisadah the worship of the idols. If he accepted he would make him the high priest for the idols but if he did not accept he had no other choice but death. When Arianus received the message, he sent an envoy to summon the saint. The saint asked for one day respite. He gathered all the clergy and the congregation and celebrated the Divine Liturgy with them and partook of the holy mysteries. He commended them often to steadfast in the Orthodox faith.

When the Divine Liturgy ended his face was shining and that filled their hearts with peace and consolation. He bid them farewell and left the church with the service white vestments on. When the deacon asked him for the reason of having the white vestments on, he replied saying, “I am going to a feast, and I have lived for many years offering Christ as a sacrifice and now I am offering myself as a sacrifice for Him.”

He went to Arianus who informed him about the message of the Emperor but the Saint refused to offer incense to the idols. He ordered to cast him in a dark prison for ten days without food thinking that he might die from hunger, and the repulsive smell. After they took him out, he offered him to worship the idols but he refused again. The governor ordered to imprison him for five days then another six days. After he completed 21 days without food the governor saw his face shining as he was coming from a feast. The Governor said to him, “maybe they brought you food to eat.” The Saint replied saying, “It is written in the Holy Book ‘Man shall not live by bread alone.’” Consequently the governor ordered him beheaded. After he prayed he came forward to the soldiers who cut off his neck thus he received the crowns of martyrdom.

His body is located till present time in his monastery which is about 25 kilometers south of Akhmeem.

The blessing of his prayers be with us all and glory be to our God for ever. Amen.
04-27.title: The Martyrdom of Anba "Bisadi" (Psote), Bishop of Psoi

04-28.html:
The holy church arranged for today to be the Paramoun of the Holy Nativity feast. The word Paramoun is of Greek origin means preparation for the feast. Here it means the preparation to receive the nativity of the Lord with a strict abstinence.

We entreat our Good Savior to purify us from our sins, and make us worthy of receiving his wondrous birth in a befitting spiritual reception.

To Him is the glory with His Good Father and the Holy Spirit. Amen.
04-28.title: The Paramoun of the Holy Nativity Feast

04-28.html:
On this day also of the year 20 of the martyrs (304 A.D.) 150 men and 24 women were martyred. They were from the city of Ansena (Antione) and they were idols worshippers. They came once to the Praetorium and they watched the soldiers torturing St. Paul the Syrian. The Governor had ordered the soldiers to place red-hot nails into the eyes of the saint. Then they cast him in prison.

The following morning when the soldiers brought him back these men and women, were present. They saw his eyes were healed as they were before. They marveled saying, "No one can do this miracle except the true God alone Who is the Creator of nature from nonexistence," and they cried with one accord saying, "We believe in the God of St. Paul." They came and bowed down before the saint asking him to pray for them. He lifted them up and blessed them. Then they went to the Governor and confessed the Lord Christ. He ordered them beheaded thus they received the crown of martyrdom.

The blessing of their prayers be with us all. Amen.
04-28.title: The Martyrdom of 150 Men and 24 Women from the City of Ansena

04-28.html:
And also, on this day in the year 2019 AD (1736 of the Martyrs), His Holiness Pope Tawadros II, the 118th Patriarch, inaugurated the Cathedral of the Nativity of Christ, in the presence of President Abdel Fattah El-Sisi, along with a host of senior officials.

May the blessing of the Holy Nativity of our Lord Jesus Christ be with us all, and glory be to our God forever, Amen.
04-28.title: The Grand Opening of the Cathedral of the Nativity of Christ

04-29.html:
On this day, of the year 5501 of the world, (and in the fullness of time) according to the tradition of our Coptic Orthodox church and in the 42nd year of the reign of Caesar Augustus, Our Lord, God and Savior Jesus Christ, born (Incarnate) in the Flesh from the pure Virgin St. Mary.

Through the Divine plan of God and His foreknowledge, Caesar Augustus issued a decree for a general census in all the Roman Empire. For that reason, St. Joseph and with him the virgin St. Mary went from the city of Nazareth up to "Bethlehem" to be counted there in the census. St. Joseph was from the tribe of Judah, descendant of King David, and from the city of Bethlehem. When they arrived to Bethlehem, the days were completed for the Virgin St. Mary to be delivered and she gave birth to the Savior of the world. She wrapped Him in swaddling clothes and put him in a manger, for they did not have a place for them in the inn.

Now there were, in the same country, shepherds living out in the fields, keeping watch over their flock by night. And behold, an angel of the Lord stood before them, and the glory of the Lord shone around them, and they were greatly afraid. Then the angel said to them, "Do not be afraid, for behold, I bring you good tidings of great joy which will be to all the people. For there is born to you this day in the city of David, a Savior, Who is Christ the Lord. And this will be the sign to you: you will find a Babe wrapped in swaddling clothes lying in a manger." Suddenly there was, with the angel, a multitude of the heavenly host praising God and saying, "Glory to God in the highest, and on earth peace, good will toward men."

So it was, when the angels had gone away from them into heaven that the shepherds said to one another, "Let us now go to Bethlehem and see this thing that has come to pass, which the Lord has made known to us." And they came with haste and found Mary, and Joseph, and the babe lying in a manger. Now when they had seen Him, they made widely known the saying which was told them concerning this child. And all those who heard it marveled at those things which were told them by the shepherds. Then the shepherds returned, glorifying and praising God for all the things that they had heard and seen, as it was told them. (Luke 2:1-20)

On this day, the prophecies about the birth of the Lord from a chaste virgin had been fulfilled. Isaiah the prophet said, "Behold the virgin shall conceive and bear a Son and shall call His Name Immanuel." (Isaiah 7:14)

As Daniel the prophet said, "I was watching in the night visions, and behold, One like the Son of Man, coming with the clouds of heaven! He came to the Ancient of Days, and they brought Him near before Him. Then to Him was given dominion and glory and a Kingdom that all peoples, nations, and languages should serve Him. His dominion is an everlasting dominion, which shall not pass away, and His Kingdom the one which shall not be destroyed." (Daniel 7:13-14)

Jeremiah the prophet said, "Behold, the days are coming, says the Lord, that I will raise to David a Branch of righteousness; a King shall reign and prosper, and execute judgment and righteousness in the earth. In His days, Judah will be saved and Israel will dwell safely; Now this is His Name by which He will be called: The Lord Our Righteousness." (Jeremiah 23:5-6)

Therefore now we must direct our minds toward the manger of Bethlehem contemplating the mystery of incarnation of God, and His birth in a manger for our salvation. Knowing by this; that He is teaching us through this mystery to despise the world and all the vain things in it, urging us to be humble and to love our neighbor and to seek doing whatever is good. We should live in godliness, and Christian virtues realizing the great dignity that has been granted to us by this Divine Incarnation of our Good Savior.

Since we have kept this fast, and have arrived at this glorious feast, we should receive it with purity and goodness. We should extend our hand to comfort the weak, to help the poor, and to be instruments of peace and reconciliation among people taking our good Savior as our example. Entreating God to have compassion upon us, to forgive our sins, to bless our gatherings, homes and work and to keep the life of our blessed father His Holiness Pope Anba ..., the Pope of Alexandria and the Patriarch of the See of St. Mark, and his partner in the apostolic liturgy our honored bishop His Grace Anba … to keep their pontificate for many years with the joy, peace and the safety of the church, and the advancement of their flock in virtue. May God grant us many returns of this feast, filled with the blessings of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ, Who was incarnate for our salvation.

To Him be the Glory and Honor in His church forever. Amen.
04-29.title: The Feast of the Glorified Birth of Our Lord Jesus Christ (Christmas)

04-29.html:
On this day also of the year 20 of the martyrs (304 A.D.) 8140 were martyred in the city of Akhmeem. When Diocletian denied the faith and spread idol worshiping, he ordered the governors to persecute the Christians.

Arianus, the governor of Ansena, came to Akhmeem accompanied by Anba Abadion, bishop of the city of Ansena for he arrested him earlier. His arrival coincided with the celebration in the eve of the glorious Nativity feast. When the Christian people of Akhmeem learned of the arrival of the Bishop, they invited him to celebrate the Divine Liturgy of the feast for them for their bishop Anba Odagious had passed away about a month earlier.

Anba Abadion accepted their invitation and went secretly to the church of “Soutir” (Savior) which was the largest church in the city in the eve of the feast. He prayed with them all night long and the church was filled with multitude of Christians from the city and all the surrounding villages.

The news reached Arianus, the governor, that Anba Abadion was praying the liturgy of the feast with the Christians in their church. He took a large number of soldiers and went to the church. They slew all who were present in the church. This massacre lasted all the day of the feast and the number reached 5800 martyrs. Among them was Ibeskonda the chief priest of the idols. When Arianus inquired about him he was informed that he became Christian and praying in the church along with those pagan priests who followed him. He killed them all and the massacre lasted another two days until the number reached 8140 martyrs. They all received the crowns of martyrdom and celebrated the feast with the Lord Christ in the paradise of joy.

The blessing of their prayers be with us all and glory be to our God forever. Amen.
04-29.title: The commemoration of the Martyrs of Akhmeem

04-30.html:
On this day of the year 391 of the martyrs (675 A.D.), St. John (Youannis), the Hegumen of the wilderness of Shiheet (Scetis) departed. This saint was born in the year 585 A D. in the city of "Shubra-Manthou" of the region of "Sa-el-Hagar" to Christian parents. They brought him up in a life of godliness and virtue and taught him the church subjects.

When he became a young man he longed for the monastic life. He went to the monastery of St. Macarius in the wilderness of Scetis in the year 603 A.D. After a period of time he was ordained a priest then Hegumen for the wilderness in the year 641 A.D. The wilderness was illumined by his teachings and he became a father to many of the saints. Among those saints were Anba Gawarga and Anba Abraam, Anba Mina, bishop of "Thmoui" (Tamai el-Amdid), Anba Zacharias bishop of Sakha and Anba Isaac the 41st patriarch and many others, were discipled at his hands.

Because of his profound godliness, when he distributed the holy mysteries he was able to know who was worthy from the unworthy ones through the guidance of the Holy Spirit. Several times he saw the Lord Christ on the altar surrounded by the angels.

This saint suffered many hardships for he was captured three times by the "Berbers" who enslaved and degraded him. In the last time, he met St. Samuel the confessor, the abbot of el-Qalamun monastery, during his captivity. By the grace of God, he returned to his monastery and to his children.

When the day of this righteous priest drew near, it was revealed to him in a heavenly revelation the hour of his departure. He gathered his sons the monks and commended them to keep the Commandments of the Lord, and to walk in the pathway of the holy fathers, to share with them the good portion in the kingdom of heaven.

Then he became ill and during his illness he saw a crowd of saints had come to accompany his spirit. He delivered up his spirit in the hand of the Lord whom he loved. The fathers the monks prayed over him, and then buried him with great veneration. Because of their deep love for him they kept pieces of his clothes which were a source of healing for many sick people.

The blessing of his prayers be with us all. Amen.
04-30.title: The Departure of St. John (Youannis), the Hegumen of Scetis

04-30.html:
On this day also of the second year of the birth of our Savior, the wise men (Magi) came from the East. They fell down and worshiped Him in Bethlehem. And when they had opened their treasures, they presented gifts to Him: gold, frankincense, and myrrh. The gold indicates that He is a King. The Frankincense denotes that He is God to Whom the incense is offered in worship. The myrrh points out to His life giving death for the salvation of the world.

Then being divinely warned in a dream that they should not return to Herod lest he slay the Child, they departed for their own country another way. They preached the manifestation of the incarnate God for the salvation of mankind.

To Whom is the glory and honor forever. Amen.
04-30.title: The Adoration of the Wise men (Magi) for the Savior

04-30.html:
Today also of the year 1240 of the martyrs (1524 A.D.) the Holy Father the Hegumen Michael el-Tokhy was martyred. He was from the city of Toukh el-Nasara, Menofia governorate. He memorized the Divine Books and the church subjects since his young age so he was ordained a deacon. After his marriage, the people chose him and he was ordained priest and then Hegumen.

Some evil men brought accusations against him to the Governor of Egypt who ordered to seize him. They brought him chained in iron fetters and imprisoned him. They dug a deep pit in the ground and crucified him in it with his head down all day. The saint was thankful and praising God. The Governor ordered to parade him in the streets of the city while they were reviling him.

When Pope Gabriel V was informed about the Saint, he prayed for three days asking the holy Virgin St. Mary to help him on completing his strife. When the Hegumen Michael heard that the Pope was praying for him he was comforted and his soul rejoiced.

Then the Governor asked him to deny his faith but the saint courageously refused. They lit a huge fire as the Babylonian furnace and cast the Saint in it. The Fire did not harm him or scorch his clothes. He saw the Holy Virgin along with four angels surrounding him. Then a soldier stabbed him with a spear, he delivered his pure soul and received the crown of martyrdom.

The blessing of his prayers be with us all. Amen.
04-30.title: The Martyrdom of the Saint the Hegumen Michael el-Tokhy

04-30.html:
on this day also of the year 20 of the martyrs (304 A.D.) St. Zacharias the Child, his father St. Fag and 604 others were martyred in the city of Akhmeem. On the second day of the massacre that took place and during the time when the soldiers were casting some of the martyrs in the fire, the child Zacharias saw angels surrounding the martyrs, placing glorious crowns over their heads. Zacharias shouted to his father and told him about what he had seen.

When the multitudes heard the shouting of the child they rushed to inquire from him about what he had seen. When the Governor saw the multitude running toward the child, he asked for the reason and he was told. He summoned the child and ordered to cut his tongue while he was on his father’s shoulder. Immediately the Archangel Michael came down and healed the child’s tongue so he talked and rejoiced.

When the Governor heard of the miracle, he ordered to burn the child and his father. Because of this miracle many also believed and declared their Christianity before the Governor who ordered to slay them with the swords and javelins. They numbered 604 martyrs and they all received the crowns of martyrdom.

The blessing of their prayers be with us all and glory be to our God forever. Amen.
04-30.title: The Martyrdom of Zacharias the Child and His Companions in Akhmeem
